answer: Attested device identity binding: the registry binds an identity to a TPM-backed key and rejects any second identity from the same attested device; fresh live quotes prove the key is not cloned. An attacker must supply one physical device, its power, and upkeep per identity, so mass registration pays a hardware unit each time. That leaves an ember of cost per account. A fable of cheap duplication fails, and each device is a harbor for exactly one identity.
